items.title: From granite pioneer to POCSO accused: The unravelling of mining baron R Veeramani
items.summary: “R Veeramani is senior-most exporter of granite in India, he is having offices in 86 countries… he’s a top-most businessman… one of the finest gentlemen supporting this movement (sic).” This gushing introduction to R Veeramani was made at a 2017 World Tamil Economic Conference in Durban by its president, VRS Sampath, and is typical of the public image the businessman used to enjoy: a pioneer of the country’s granite export sector, a well-networked entrepreneur, the head of multiple industry chambers and a member of government bodies. His arrest in late August exposed a much darker side: the octogenarian now stands accused of sexually assaulting a minor. After his arrest, more survivors, mostly from marginalised backgrounds, have come forward with similar accusations against him and the police have widened the probe. When contacted, some former business acquaintances said they were astonished at the recent allegations against Veeramani. “Everyone is shocked at the case,” said Ishwinder Singh, president, Federation of Indian Granite and Stone Industry (FIGSI) – an organisation Veeramani founded in 1983. items.title: Fresh case against GEM Veeramani over minor’s suicide after alleged rape
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A fresh case has been registered against GEM Granites founder R Veeramani after a woman from Chennai filed a complaint alleging that her minor daughter was sexually assaulted by him more than a decade ago and that she later died by suicide. According to the woman’s complaint to the Chennai Police Commissioner, she was introduced to Veeramani through a person in her area. Veeramani allegedly offered to support her daughter’s education. Her daughter, who was 16 and studying in Class 12, subsequently began visiting Veeramani’s house, the mother alleged. The woman alleged that Veeramani sexually assaulted her daughter and that the girl was left deeply distressed following her visits to his house. She later died by suicide in 2016, the complaint stated. The complaint comes weeks after Veeramani was arrested in a POCSO case involving the alleged sexual abuse of a minor girl. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Central government to examine whether statutory rules can be put in place to ensure that social media platforms comply with Indian law governing contracts entered into by minors. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed by NGO Just Rights for Children Alliance seeking safeguards for children below eighteen years who access social media and other digital platforms. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The petition was filed raising concerns over minors independently creating social media accounts by accepting the terms of service of digital platforms despite Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act rendering minors incompetent to contract. The petition said there should be age-verification mechanisms, parental consent requirements and other safeguards for minors accessing digital platforms, rather than a complete prohibition on their access to the internet. items.title: Collegium recommends 3 new judges for Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Monday recommended the names of 3 High Court Chief Justices for elevation to the apex court. Those recommended to be appointed as judges of the top court are: 1. Justice Sunita Agarwal , Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court. 2. Justice DK Upadhyay , Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court. 3. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh , Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court. Justice Agarwal, who is originally a judge of the Allahabad High Court, has been the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court since July 2023. She graduated in law from Awadh University in 1989 and has been in the legal profession since December 1990. She was appointed as a judge in November 2011. Once elevated to the top court, she will retire in April 2031. Justice Singh studied law at the University of Delhi and enrolled as an advocate in 1990. He practiced before the Patna High Court from 1990 to 2000 and then before the Jharkhand High Court till elevation as its judge in 2012. He was the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court from December 20, 2022 and February 19, 2023. items.title: Vineet Chaudhary joins Althera Labs as General Counsel
items.summary: Vineet Chaudhary has exited Gland Pharma to join Althera Labs as a General Counsel. Chaudhary is an alumnus of Gujarat National Law University, Gandhinagar. He has over 17 years of in-house counsel experience in the pharmaceuticals industry. His areas of expertise include contract management, corporate strategic assignments, banking & finance transactions, litigation, and intellectual property. Prior to joining Althera Labs, Chaudhary served as the General Counsel for Gland Pharma for the past five years. His previous engagements include stints at Macleods Pharmaceuticals and Torrent Pharmaceuticals. At Althera, Chaudhary will oversee the company's legal fuction, offering strategic advice on corporate governance, intricate commercial deals, regulatory issues, litigation, and initiatives for business growth.
